erin: Heads-up — noticed a spike in billing-tag:fncall on hosted route svc-payroll. Many requests show as SUCCESS but the tool never ran. Feels like validator soft-reject + silent fallback to a non-tooling model. Anyone seen this?
jordan: saw that too. logs show validator returning reject, orchestrator then rerouted to fallback variant that strips tools. we still charged both attempts. pasting example log below.
```
2026-03-22T14:02:45Z ERROR validate_fncall payload_id=abc123 route=svc-payroll model=gptx-13b validator=fncall-v2 reason=missing_required_field fallback_route=svc-payroll-lite cost_tokens=142
2026-03-22T14:02:45Z INFO router reroute original_route=svc-payroll -> fallback=svc-payroll-lite billing_tag=TOKEN_CHARGE
```
kai: ugh. that matches what I saw. billing pipeline gets the final billing_tag but the first attempt already produced token usage. so customers see one successful response but double cost.
maria: can we change routing policy to NOT fallback to variants that strip tooling? fallback should either return a validation error to client or route to a variant that preserves tool hooks. silent fallback is dangerous.
erin: +1. console also misleading — route shows success and no indication that fncall was suppressed. product should display "fncall suppressed by schema validator" in the per-request detail.
jordan: quick mitigation: add a sampled flag for these events and create a dashboard panel showing validation_outcome vs billing_delta. I'll add sampling_tags: fncall_validation=reject,fallbacked=true.
kai: also we need to carry a separate billing_metadata field through orchestrator -> billing so we can attribute token charges to the attempt type (validation_attempt vs fallback_attempt). right now it's overwritten on reroute.
maria: proposal: add customer opt-in flag strict_fncall: if true, validator rejections return 400 to client (no fallback, no extra model hit). default false for compatibility. enterprise customers can enable strict to avoid silent masking.
erin: that seems reasonable. UX note: console toggle should include explanation of tradeoffs (availability vs correctness).
jordan: I'll draft the console toggle and a canary plan. plan: roll strict_fncall to dedicated accounts first then 10% hosted. will also wire up the dashboard panel and sampling.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout scheduled for fncall-strict-2026-03-22 -> 10% hosted accounts, start=2026-03-22T15:00:00Z (canary_id=fncall-strict-2026-03-22).
erin: next steps: jordan -> dashboard + sampling tag PR, kai -> billing metadata patch, maria -> UX copy + toggle PR. I'll own rollout coordination and QA. sync in 30m?
jordan: created ENG-4217 to track dashboard + sampling work. will ping once query is live.
kai: will open billing PR and add tests to ensure billing_tag is append-only when rerouting.
maria: will draft UX copy and wire the toggle behind a console feature flag.
erin: thanks all. low-sev but high-customer-impact; want this in next minor.
